([[Powder Springs, Georgia]]) | college = [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]] (2020–2021) | highlights = * [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] All-Freshman Team (2021) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2020 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2020]]) * [[Jordan Brand Classic]] (2020) * [[USA Today All-USA high school basketball team#Boys' basketball players and coaches of the year|''USA Today'' All-USA Player of the Year]] (2019) * [[Mr. Georgia Basketball]] (2019) | medal_templates = }} '''Sharife Omar Cooper''' (born June 11, 2001) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn Tigers]]. ==High school career== In his freshman season in 2016–17, Cooper averaged 16 points and 4.4 assists per game, leading [[McEachern High School]] in [[Powder Springs, Georgia]] to a 29–1 record and an appearance in the [[Georgia High School Association]] (GHSA) Class 7A state semifinals. The following year, he led the Indians to a state quarterfinals appearance while posting a 26–3 record.{{cite news|url=https://davesjoint.net/2018/06/06/hoop-with-coop-a-point-guard-from-georgia-gives-the-world-an-introduction/|title=Hoop With Coop: A Point Guard from Georgia Gives The World An Introduction|first=David|last=Cordova|publisher=Dave's Joint|date=June 6, 2018|accessdate=July 27, 2019}} He received considerable media attention in December 2017 for his 42-point performance against [[Jahvon Quinerly]] and nationally ranked [[Hudson Catholic Regional High School]] in the quarterfinals of the [[City of Palms Classic]]. He scored the game-winning buzzer-beater in an 83–81 [[overtime (sports)|overtime]] victory.{{cite news|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/FvJAXXeXyEq2SZgow2GNEw/sharife-coopers-42-point-performance-highlights-early-going-at-city-of-palms-classic.htm|title=Sharife Cooper's 42-point performance highlights early going at City of Palms Classic|first=Lynden|last=Ostrander|publisher=MaxPreps|date=December 21, 2017|accessdate=July 27, 2019}}{{cite news|url=https://hoopseen.com/news/event/201712/cooper-has-epic-outing-ot-mceachern-win|title=Cooper Has Epic Outing in OT McEachern Win|first=Justin|last=Young|publisher=HoopSeen|date=December 20, 2017|accessdate=July 27, 2019}} As a junior in 2018–19, Cooper led McEachern to a perfect 32–0 record and the first state title in school history while averaging 27.2 points, 8.1 assists, 5.6 rebounds and 4.3 steals per game. In the title-game win over [[Meadowcreek High School|Meadowcreek]], he scored 20 points and dished four assists as McEachern finished ranked No. 1 in three national polls.{{cite news|url=https://www.ajc.com/blog/high-school-sports/aaaaaaa-basketball-blog-mceachern-westlake-finish-unbeaten-nationally-ranked/xC00FOEfhm6RguahaYHm0H/|title=AAAAAAA basketball blog: McEachern, Westlake finish unbeaten, nationally ranked|first=Todd|last=Holcomb|publisher=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]|date=March 12, 2019|accessdate=July 28, 2019}} He picked up [[most valuable player]] (MVP) honors at several tournaments, including the City of Palms Classic and Tournament of Champions.{{cite news|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/hiEtJCTmEUuugDTFsLy1Ng/sharife-cooper-leads-race-for-high-school-basketball-player-of-the-year-honors.htm|title=Sharife Cooper leads race for high school basketball player of the year honors|first=Jordan|last=Divens|publisher=[[MaxPreps]]|date=January 31, 2019|accessdate=July 26, 2019}} After the season, he was named [[USA Today All-USA high school basketball team|''USA Today'' All-USA Player of the Year]], [[MaxPreps National Basketball Player of the Year awards|MaxPreps National Player of the Year]], [[Mr. Georgia Basketball]], and Georgia's [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]].{{cite news|url=https://usatodayhss.com/2019/2018-19-all-usa-boys-basketball-player-of-the-year-sharife-cooper-mceachern|title=2018-19 ALL-USA Boys Basketball Player of the Year: Sharife Cooper, news|url=https://www.mdjonline.com/sports/mceachern-s-sharife-cooper-named-second-team-all-american/article_bbfb2454-4202-11e9-8263-d3d0186a4135.html|title=McEachern's Sharife Cooper named second-team All-American|first=Adam|last=Carrington|publisher=[[Marietta Daily Journal]]|date=March 8, 2019|accessdate=July 26, 2019}} Cooper was selected to play in the [[2020 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]] on January 23, 2020.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28548029/four-north-carolina-signees-dot-mcdonald-all-american-game-rosters|title=Four UNC signees dot All-American Game rosters|date=2020-01-23|website=ESPN.com|language=en|access-date=2020-01-23}} On May 6, 2021, Cooper's #2 high school jersey number was retired at McEachern where he was honored as the most decorated male basketball player in school history.{{cite web|url=https://auburnwire.usatoday.com/2021/05/09/look-sharife-cooper-has-high-school-number-retired/|title=Look Sharife Cooper has high school number retired|date=2021-05-09|website=auburnwire.usatoday.com|language=en|access-date=2021-05-09}} ===Recruiting=== On September 27, 2019, Cooper committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]]. He became the highest-ranked recruit and the second five-star recruit in program history.{{cite web |last1=Green |first1=Tom |title=5-star point guard Sharife Cooper commits to Auburn |url=https://www.al.com/alabamabasketball/2019/09/5-star-point-guard-sharife-cooper-commits-to-auburn.html |website=AL.com |accessdate=September 27, 2019 |date=September 27, 2019}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2020}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Sharife Cooper | position = [[Point guard|PG]] | hometown = [[Powder Springs, Georgia|Powder Springs, GA]] | highschool = [[McEachern High School|McEachern]] (GA) | feet = 6 | inches = 0 | weight = 160 | 40 = | commitdate = September 27, 2019 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 94 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2020 | rivals ref title = Auburn 2020 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2020 Auburn Tigers Recruiting Class | rivals school = auburn | scout s = | espn schoolid = 2 | 247 overall = 27 | rivals overall = 22 | espn overall = 20 | accessdate = October 14, 2020 | bball = yes }} ==College career== Cooper missed the first 12 games of his freshman season due to a [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] investigation into his eligibility. During that time, he explored professional options.{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Auburn Tigers freshman Sharife Cooper cleared by NCAA, to make debut Saturday |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/30679440/auburn-tigers-freshman-sharife-cooper-cleared-ncaa-make-debut-saturday |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=April 16, 2021 |date=January 9, 2021}} On January 9, 2021, he made his Auburn debut, recording 26 points, nine assists and four rebounds in a 94–90 loss to [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]].{{cite web |last1=Han |first1=Giana |title=Sharife Cooper's debut encouraging for Auburn despite loss |url=https://www.al.com/auburnbasketball/2021/01/sharife-coopers-debut-encouraging-for-auburn-despite-loss.html |website=AL.com |access-date=April 16, 2021 |date=January 9, 2021}} Four days later, Cooper posted a season-high 28 points, 12 assists and five rebounds in a 95–77 win over [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia]].{{cite web |title=Cooper dominant again as Auburn beats Georgia 95-77 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401258746 |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=April 16, 2021 |date=January 13, 2021}} As a freshman, he averaged 20.2 points, 8.1 assists and 4.3 rebounds per game through 12 appearances, earning [[Southeastern Conference]] All-Freshman Team honors. After the season, Cooper declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] and chose to forgo his remaining eligibility.{{cite web |title=Auburn's Sharife Cooper to enter NBA draft, hire agent |url=https://www.nba.com/news/auburns-sharife-cooper-to-enter-nba-draft-hire-agent |website=NBA.com |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=April 16, 2021 |date=April 2, 2021}} ==Career
